title: Mental health among children and youngsters in Kosovo
abstract: Background: Child and adolescent mental health remains under-researched and insufficiently addressed in many developing countries, including Kosovo, highlighting the need to consider the influence of social and cultural dynamics. Objective: The current study investigated the mental health of children and adolescents, taking into account the social and cultural factors that may influence their well-being. Methods: A mixed-methods design, equally weighted, was employed. The quantitative study included 318 participants. Data were collected using a demographic questionnaire and the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire. The qualitative study included 36 participants, who were interviewed using semi-structured interviews. Results: The findings showed that 38.7% of participants scored emotional problems above the normal range. In the same range, but with different % is also conduct problems 84.6%, hyperactivity 73.6% and peer problems 93.2%. Qualitative findings highlighted difficulties in identifying the early signs of psychological problems and emphasized the important role of families, teachers, and peers in helping children and adolescents cope with psychological difficulties. Conclusion: The findings indicate a clear need to increase public awareness of psychological problems, as well as to strengthen professional mental health services. Furthermore, there is a need to create supportive environments within families and schools that encourage open discussion of psychosocial difficulties and promote early identification and intervention.
